summary: Greedy menus of (u,C) pairs: 8, 33, 112 items for primes ≡1 (24) in [10^3,2·10^3), [10^4,2·10^4), [10^5,2·10^5) with u ≤ 400. Cap sweep at k=4 (u ≤ 100/400/1500) gives 33 items for all caps, so the growth is not a cap artifact at that scale (k=5 cap sweep not run). Menu size grows roughly ×3.5–4 per decade: no bounded universal menu in this range.

Gowers/Nikolov–Pyber size check for SL₂(F_p): |A||B||C| ≈ p³ against |G|³/m ≈ p⁸ (deficit ≈ p⁵). The reduction mod q is far from the Gowers threshold; the same arithmetic appears in H05 (Z1915, Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao lane).

FRONTIER.md §1–2: the expected number of solutions per prime is polylogarithmic in p, and power-size C adds only a log-power in A. Our data show that the minimal C is >√p for only 0.1% of primes, so a power-size reservoir is not needed for most p.

Multiplicative energy of divisor classes of N=(p+7)/4 mod 7 (normalised by |D|^2) for 25 hard primes ≤ 2·10^4: mean 21.53 vs 22.66 for random N of the same size (5 controls each). No excess; nothing usable.

Problem 308 (solved by Croot): smallest integer not a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators ≤N; Croot's bound. Subset-sum, no ES content. Lookup via erdosproblems.com page (status and statement read); the cited papers were not read in full.

Abstract read (arXiv 1904.00290, LMMS): effective avoidance for unipotent orbits. The ES equation 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) is not a fixed homogeneous form equal to a constant, so the counting theorem does not apply directly.

Searched for an Erdős remark that congruence covers cannot settle 4/n and for Erdős–Graham's unit-fraction discussion: the results were secondary pages (Wikipedia, Tao's blog, a congruence-system preprint). No primary Erdős remark was found, so the item's premise remains unverified.
(4uC-1) | (p+u) is the trial form of R(p) in FRONTIER §2.1.
The first step needs a map from a totally positive cyclotomic unit eta (eta = -1 mod an inert prime) to an ES solution, and the item gives no such map. Not executable as stated.

Kronecker–Hurwitz identity Σ_t H(4n−t²) = 2σ(n) − Σ_{d|n} min(d,n/d) verified numerically for n≤12 with a reduced-form class-number count (weights 1/2, 1/3, H(0)=−1/12). The Type I sums Σ_c H(p²+4c²d) vary the discriminant with c and are not of this fixed-n shape, so no trace identity for ES is found.
Density of states over (u, C) with u, C ≤ 20 and p ≡ 1 (mod 4) in (10^3, 3·10^3): gcd(p+u, 4uC−1) = 1 for 79.7% of the 52400 triples; the defect distribution is 3 (9.9%), 5 (3.1%), 7 (1.8%).

The attempts at Lefschetz-type fixed-point arguments on a certificate space are recorded in BRAINSTORM/invol_topological.md (file exists in the repo; not re-read in this pass). The item asks for the same maps, so nothing new is claimed here.
